_doc: ExO 3.0 field failure catalog for Exos Aerospace. Each entry records a real governance or execution failure, mapped to the ExO3 skill vocabulary. Source: logs/exo3-gate.jsonl, state/agent-eval-state.json, mission-control/data/improvement-ledger.json, lessons-learned.md, memory/ feedback_* files, git log. Maintained by scripts/exo3_field_report.py (weekly).

failures.title: 9 live agents slipped past commit gate via out-of-git plist loading
failures.what_happened: 9 live launchd agents were running in ~/Library/LaunchAgents/ and had been started via launchctl, but their plist files were never staged to git. The pre-commit gate (exo3_gate.py) only inspects staged additions, so these agents operated outside the registry for an unknown period — no owner, no eval, no accountability.
failures.root_cause: The commit-gate checks staged diffs but has no visibility into the runtime LaunchAgents directory. A deployment step (launchctl load) outside git is a blind spot.
failures.structural_fix: agent_eval.py hourly registry-drift check: compares ~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.exos.* + launchctl list against agent-registry.json; sends one deduped Discord alert per NEW unregistered agent. Result stored in state/agent-eval-state.json _registry_drift key. 9 agents backfilled with full specs.

failures.title: Liveness-only evals: 0/136 side-effecting agents had output evals (now 69/136, 50.7%)
failures.what_happened: On 2026-10-04 every agent's registry eval was liveness/exit-code only (loaded + LastExitStatus=0 + staleness). An agent can run, exit 0, and still produce wrong outputs (duplicate sends, missed deliverables, stale data) without any eval catching it. The decisions-discord-feed triple-post (F-003) is a direct consequence.
failures.root_cause: The initial eval rollout (Eval Wave 1, 2026-09-20) defaulted all agents to liveness checks. The AGENT_SPEC_SCHEMA does not mandate an output eval for side-effecting agents. Only 27/238 (11%) have explicit output evals.
failures.structural_fix: Gate R5 (f2c7e2a) blocks new side-effecting agents that only have a liveness eval. Registry backfill gave 69 deliver.py senders the generic duplicate-send output eval. The 67 agents that send or write via msmtp/Supabase/QB still need bespoke output evals. Framework fix: AGENT_SPEC_SCHEMA should require output_eval for side-effecting agents.
failures.evidence: config/agent-evals.json (238 agents, 155 liveness-only), improvement-ledger.json IMP-008, fleet-events.jsonl dup_send events 2026-10-04

failures.title: decisions-discord-feed triple-posted — shared-lib retry on CLI timeout
failures.what_happened: decisions-discord-feed posted 3 copies of the same Decision card to Discord. Root cause: deliver.py (shared send library) treated an OpenClaw CLI timeout as a failed delivery and retried. The message had already landed. No output eval existed to detect dup_sends before this session.
failures.root_cause: Two compounding gaps: (1) deliver.py's retry logic did not treat CLI timeout as 'at-most-once delivered'; (2) the agent's only eval was liveness — no duplicate-send output eval existed. The shared library's behavior change had fleet-wide blast radius (50+ agents use deliver.py).
failures.structural_fix: IMP-003 (delivery-sweeper inline-grace 218s skips files fresh enough to still be in-flight); IMP-008 (at-most-once: CLI timeout treated as delivered, plus dup_send output eval added to agent_eval.py). Registry updated with output eval in eval_suite.
failures.evidence: fleet-events.jsonl dup_send events 2026-10-04T17:39-41, improvement-ledger.json IMP-003 + IMP-008, commit 0a386e9

failures.title: ETA promises ran 7-11x too long — no calibration feedback loop
failures.what_happened: Jon observed that Exo's promised turnaround ETAs consistently ran 7-11x longer than actual task completion times. There was no measurement, no logging, and no recursive correction — the Trust Loop was open. Users cannot calibrate trust in an agent whose self-estimates are systematically wrong.
failures.root_cause: No logging of promised vs. actual turnaround; no weekly audit of ETA accuracy; default estimates were based on model intuition, not calibrated baselines.
failures.structural_fix: scripts/eta_log.py add --task ... --kind quick|edit|research|build --promised N --actual M; weekly RSI §14 flags drift and proposes new defaults. AGENTS.md hardcodes calibrated defaults (5/10/20/40 min by kind, pad at most 20%).

failures.title: Stale carry-forward flags escalated to Jon without source re-verification
failures.what_happened: Capture agents and the main agent were flagging Jon with alerts and escalations that were stale — the underlying condition had already changed or been resolved. Jon was receiving attention-demanding notifications for issues that no longer required his input.
failures.root_cause: No re-verification step before escalating to Jon. The Fiduciary Wedge (only route to Jon what genuinely requires his decision) was not enforced operationally.
failures.structural_fix: memory feedback_jon_attention_gate.md: capture agents verify at source before flagging Jon; no stale carry-forward. Any captured flag must be re-checked against live state before posting to the Decisions board.

failures.title: claude-cli toolsAllow cron trap — injected allow-list silently killed crons
failures.what_happened: Editing a cron via the cron MCP tool from a claude-cli session auto-injected toolsAllow from the calling session's allowlist. The claude-cli backend cannot enforce runtime toolsAllow and errors immediately (~170ms) with 'CLI backend cannot enforce runtime toolsAllow'. The cron appeared loaded and had no errors in launchctl, but produced zero output — classic Quiet Drift. First detected 2026-07-20 for R-017; recurred fleet-wide 2026-08-25 after a model-bump re-injected toolsAllow across 10 anthropic/* crons.
failures.root_cause: OpenClaw cron tool side-effect: cron creation/edit from a claude-cli session inherits the session's toolsAllow. The claude-cli backend treats this as a configuration error. No gate prevented injection; no eval caught the near-instant failure pattern.
failures.structural_fix: `openclaw cron edit <id> --clear-tools` removes toolsAllow. RULE: never leave toolsAllow on an anthropic/* cron. Any model-bump/edit of an anthropic cron must be followed by --clear-tools. ollama/* crons unaffected (embedded backend enforces tools cleanly).

failures.title: UTD capstone answerer false self-post — 7/7 questions silently failed
failures.what_happened: 7 of 7 UTD capstone questions (tasks #3357-3363) showed ANSWERED status in MC but had not been posted to Discord. The agent returned marked text claiming ANSWERED, but had no posting tools available in its execution context and reported success without any external verification. Students received no responses for 2 days.
failures.root_cause: Agentic Fidelity Paradox: the agent's self-reported status (ANSWERED) was disconnected from actual external outcome (Discord post landed + DB row verified). No output eval checked the Discord delivery or the DB row after the agent ran.
failures.structural_fix: IMP-007: script validates, posts externally, verifies the DB row, then marks Done. 3x/15-min retry ETA watchdog. Daily stale check for questions unanswered >8h. Output eval now checks that answer delivery rate = 100% within one ETA.

failures.title: Shared-library blast radius — deliver.py change broke multiple agents simultaneously
failures.what_happened: deliver.py's retry behavior change (or interaction with CLI timeouts) propagated a duplicate-send failure to all agents using the library simultaneously. There is no dependency map; no eval monitors deliver.py's fleet-wide output; a single shared-library regression has Tier-1 blast radius across the fleet.
failures.root_cause: No dependency blast-radius analysis for shared libraries. AGENT_SPEC_SCHEMA records each agent's permission_envelope but does not require declaration of shared-library dependencies. A change to deliver.py is not flagged as a DECIDE/GOVERN-level change by the exo3 gate.
failures.structural_fix: IMP-003 (delivery-sweeper inline-grace); IMP-008 (at-most-once). Framework fix needed: add deliver.py and other critical shared libs to DECIDE_GOVERN_FILES in exo3_gate.py so changes trigger a Four-Pillars WARN. See exos-field-lessons.md.
failures.evidence: fleet-events.jsonl dup_send events 2026-10-04, improvement-ledger.json IMP-003, exo3_gate.py DECIDE_GOVERN_FILES set

failures.title: mc-email-command durable_send_shim quiet import errors — 64 silent failures
failures.what_happened: mc-email-command had 64 quiet errors from 'No module named durable_send_shim' — the module was importable in some environments but not in the cron's runtime. The agent exited 0 (liveness eval: PASS) while silently dropping email commands. Baseline: 311 runs, 79.4% reliability (64 quiet errors).
failures.root_cause: sys.path was set after the shim import; cron runtime path differs from interactive. Exit-code-only eval could not detect module import failures that the script swallowed. Unrelated 62 IMAP login errors from Mac Studio migration (9/28-29) masked the true signature count.
failures.structural_fix: IMP-002 commit 994012e: sys.path insert before shim import. Baseline confound noted (migration errors excluded from verdict). Output eval added (governance_checks in agent-evals.json).
failures.evidence: improvement-ledger.json IMP-002, commit 994012e, config/agent-evals.json mc-email-command governance_checks
